section.title: What changed and why
section.question: What important changes were made to the project, and why were they made?

evidence.excerpt: --- project: echo_field document_type: design_decision category: decisions status: current dataset_role: demo ------------------ # Echo Field — Design Decisions ## Project aim Echo Field is a responsive visual installation that explores how visual feedback based on body movement can influence a user’s sense of control and engagement. The installation uses a webcam to estimate movement intensity. This value controls the speed, density and colour of a generative visual environment. ## Initial interaction idea The initial concept focused on hand gestures as the main interaction method. Hand movements were intended to provide precise control over the visual response. ## Problem with hand tracking Early experiments showed that hand-gesture detection was inconsistent. result.note: The records explicitly document the change, its reason, and that the hand-gesture approach was superseded.

section.title: Relevant feedback
section.question: What tutor or user feedback is relevant to the current project direction?

evidence.excerpt: --- project: echo_field document_type: tutor_feedback category: feedback status: reviewed dataset_role: demo ------------------ # Echo Field — Tutor Feedback ## Context This feedback was received after a rehearsal of the responsive visual installation. ## Feedback point 1 — Connect colour to movement The visual response should not rely only on changes in speed. Colour should also change with movement intensity so that users receive more than one form of visual feedback. A possible direction was to use blue for lower movement and shift towards green or yellow-green as movement increases. ## Feedback point 2 — Explain the change in interaction method The project presentation should explain why the interaction changed from hand gestures to whole-body movement. The final research framing should

Feedback point 2 — Explain the change in interaction method The project presentation should explain why the interaction changed from hand gestures to whole-body movement. The final research framing should show that this decision emerged from practical experimentation with unstable gesture detection rather than presenting whole-body movement as an unexplained starting point. ## Feedback point 3 — Consider multiple participants The difference between one-person and multi-person interaction could be explored. Multiple bodies may produce a stronger movement signal, but this does not necessarily mean that each participant would feel an equal sense of control. ## Response to feedback The colour system was connected to movement intensity. The project documentation was revised to explain the transition from hand gestures to whole-body

result.summary: Tutor feedback asked for colour to change with movement intensity and for the presentation to explain the shift from hand gestures to whole-body movement, prompted by unstable gesture detection. The record says the colour system was connected to movement intensity and the documentation was revised to explain the transition; exploring single- versus multi-person interaction was also suggested.
result.note: The records explicitly provide relevant tutor feedback and state that two feedback points were addressed; multiple-participant interaction is described as an exploration to consider, not an unresolved issue.
